message.reasoning:
Design: gold hoop ring in XY plane, opening visible — use a ring with a gap? Ring is closed torus. To make opening visible, use a partial hoop: could use polygon? Simpler: use ring but with a gap... Ring geometry is full torus. Alternative: build hoop from a C-shape polygon extruded? Polygon extruded along Z gives flat shape; hoop lies in XY plane, so a C-shaped polygon extruded in Z with thickness = tube diameter works. But tube must be round-ish; a C-shaped outline with rounded ends is complex. Simpler: use several small cylinders arranged in arc to form open hoop? At most 12 parts.

Option: hoop as ring (torus) but with opening created by a gap: use two ring segments? Ring is full torus only. Use cylinders: arc of cylinders along circle, leaving a gap. E.g., 8 cylinders of length ~8mm arranged on radius 10mm circle, tangent to circle, leaving ~60° gap. Each cylinder axis local Z... cylinder axis is local Z, so to lie tangent in XY plane, rotate cylinder so its axis is along tangent direction (rotate 90° about X then rotate about Z). Cylinder axis local Z; rotate X by 90° makes axis along Y; then rotate Z to align tangent.

Circle radius R=10, tube radius 1.2 (diameter 2.4). Gap of ~50°. Use 7 segments covering 310°, each segment spans ~44.3°, chord length = 2R sin(22.15°)≈7.55mm. Cylinders length 8 to overlap slightly. Positions at angles θ_i = -155° + i*44.3°? Let's compute: gap centered at 90° (top). Segments centered at angles from 90+25=115° going around to 90-25=65°... covering 310°: centers at 115° + k*(310/7)=115+44.286k, k=0..6: 115,159.3,203.6,247.9,292.1,336.4,20.7°. Last at 20.7°, gap from 65° to 115° — good, opening at top.

Cylinder: size (2.4,2.4,8) local Z length 8. Rotation: rotate about X 90° → axis along Y; then rotate about Z by (θ+90°) to make axis tangent. Tangent direction at angle θ is θ+90°. So rotation_deg = [90, 0, θ+90].

Position: (R cosθ, R sinθ, 0).

Then pendant: turquoise bead (ellipsoid) hanging below, touching hoop. Bead at bottom of hoop (θ=270°): position (0, -10, 0)? Bead diameter ~6mm, center at (0, -10-? ) must touch hoop: hoop tube radius 1.2, so bead center at (0, -(10+1.2+3-1 overlap)) = bead radius 3, center at y = -(10+1.2+3-0.5)= -13.7. Total extent: hoop diameter 22.4 + bead... fits in 28mm? Hoop spans 22.4mm in XY; bead bottom at -13.7-3=-16.7 → total 33.4mm > 28. Too big.

Shrink: R=7, tube 1.0. Hoop diameter 16. Bead radius 2.5, center y = -(7+1+2.5-0.5) = -10. Bottom at -12.5. Total height 25mm, width 16. Fits 28. Good.

Recompute segments: R=7, gap 50° at top (90°). 7 segments over 310°, each 44.286°, chord = 2*7*sin(22.14°)=5.27, use length 6 for overlap. Cylinder size (2,2,6).

Positions: θ_k = 115 + 44.286k.

k0: 115°: pos (7cos115, 7sin115) = (-2.956, 6.349), rot [90,0,205]
k1: 159.29°: (-6.563, 2.449), rot Z 249.29
k2: 203.57°: (-6.411, -2.832), rot 293.57
k3: 247.86°: (-2.718, -6.451), rot 337.86
k4: 292.14°: (2.718, -6.451), rot 22.14 (382.14)
k5: 336.43°: (6.563, -2.449), rot 66.43
k6: 20.71°: (6.411? wait cos20.71=0.9354*7=6.548, sin=0.3537*7=2.476), rot 110.71

Bead: ellipsoid size (5,5,5) at (0, -10.5, 0). Distance from hoop center 10.5; hoop outer tube surface at 7+1=8 from center at bottom... bead top at -10.5+2.5=-8, hoop bottom outer at y=-8. Touching exactly; add overlap: bead at y=-10, top at -7.5, hoop tube center at -7, tube extends to -8. Overlap 0.5. Good. Bead center (0,-10,0), size 5.

Also maybe a small gold connector bead above turquoise? Keep simple: 9 parts total (7 cylinders + bead + maybe a tiny gold cap). Add a small gold cylinder connector at (0,-8,0)? The bead already touches. Fine with 8 parts. Maybe add a small gold ring at top of gap? No—opening must be visible.

Gold color (0.85,0.65,0.2), metallic 1, roughness 0.15. Turquoise (0.1,0.8,0.75), metallic 0.1, roughness 0.4.
